lines: Audio file browser and player: it streams WAV, FLAC and MP3 from disk, previews them with trim points and looping, and drags a sample onto a sampler module.
The left channel of the file being previewed.
The right channel of the file being previewed.
Sets the level of the preview, from silence to plus 6dB.
Starts playback as soon as a file is clicked in the browser; shift-clicking a file plays it whatever this is set to.
Menu — Resample on playback converts the file to Rack's sample rate as it plays, and Resample on drop converts the file handed to another module.
Menu — Folder for converted or trimmed files writes generated files next to the source, into a folder you choose, or into the patch's own storage so they travel with the patch.
Menu — Index metadata for all files reads duration, sample rate, bit depth, channels and BPM for every file in the current folder, which is what the search filters read.
Menu — Suggest tags analyses the first 30 seconds of a file and proposes tags from a fixed vocabulary of eighteen.
Note — the space bar starts and stops playback, and dragging a file onto a sampler module loads it there; a set trim region drops only that part of the file.
Turns MIDI messages into the binary signal that Expert Sleepers ESX-8GT hardware reads, giving MIDI the same sample-accurate timing as the audio interface.
Carries one MIDI port encoded as an audio-rate signal for an Expert Sleepers 8GT module; nothing else in a patch reads it.
Menu — Driver active switches on the MIDI-ESX driver, which other MIDI modules can then select as their output device.
Menu — Port group A to D picks which set of virtual MIDI ports this module receives from.
Note — output is produced only at a sample rate of 48000Hz.
A livecoding sequencer running the ORCA language: letters typed into the grid are operators that build patterns and send MIDI and CV as the frame counter advances.
A trigger advances the simulation by one frame, in place of the internal clock.
A trigger resets the frame counter to zero.
Read by the CV read operator: a numeric read maps 0-10V onto the values 0 to 35, and a pitch read gives the semitone of a volt-per-octave voltage.
Sets the speed of the internal clock, 30 to 300 beats per minute, when nothing is patched to the clock input.
Starts and stops the simulation; the space bar does the same.
Advances the simulation by one frame on each press.
Carries a trigger on every frame of the simulation.
Written by the CV write operator: a numeric write maps the values 0 to 35 onto 0-10V, and a pitch write gives a volt-per-octave voltage.
Menu — the embedded ORCA tutorial examples load straight into the grid.
Menu — the virtual MIDI ports must be enabled here before other MIDI modules can select them.
Note — a voltage written as a pitch can carry a gate length, after which it returns to 0V; without one it is held.
Restricts patching to a learned area of the rack: a module moved outside that area is disabled, and enabled again when it is moved back inside.
Menu — Learn starts a drag across the rack to mark the usable area.
Menu — a limit on the number of modules or of cables removes the most recently added ones whenever the count would be exceeded.
Stores, recalls and sequences eight snapshots of the presets of any modules bound to it, and binds several modules at once.
Short-press applies this snapshot to the bound modules, or in write mode stores their current presets into it; long-press clears it, or sets the sequence length in read mode.
Read applies a snapshot by hand, Auto stores the current presets whenever a new snapshot is selected, and Write stores the bound modules' presets into the snapshot pressed.
Selects the snapshot: a trigger steps through the slots forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, or 0-10V or a volt-per-octave note picks one outright.
A trigger restarts the snapshot sequence at the first slot.
Menu — Bind module (left) binds the module on the left, Bind module (select one) binds a module you click, and bound modules are drawn with a coloured outline.
Menu — Stability and performance picks Safe mode, which locks audio processing while a preset loads, or the two unsafe modes, which load without locking it.
Menu — Arm mode on the CV port applies a snapshot pressed by hand on the next clock trigger arriving there.
Note — fifteen +8 expanders to the right raise the total number of snapshots to 128.
EightFaceMk2.notes: The CV port also reads 0-10V or volt-per-octave notes when the menu is set to those modes, so its trigger colouring covers the default mode only.

lines: Expander adding eight more snapshot slots to 8FACE mk2, placed immediately to the right of it or of another +8.
Short-press applies this snapshot to the modules bound by 8FACE mk2, or in write mode stores their current presets into it; long-press clears it.
EightFaceMk2Ex.notes: The single output carries no position in the census and no name; it is not drawn on the panel, so it has no line.

lines: Stores, recalls and sequences eight presets of one module, placed immediately to the right of the module it manages.
Short-press applies this preset to the managed module, or in write mode stores that module's current preset into it; long-press clears it, or sets the sequence length in read mode.
Read applies a preset by hand, Auto stores the current preset whenever a new slot is selected, and Write stores the managed module's preset into the slot pressed.
Selects the preset slot: a trigger steps through the slots forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, or 0-10V or a volt-per-octave note picks one outright.
A trigger restarts the preset sequence at the first slot.
Menu — the managed module can be taken from the left instead of the right.
Menu — Stability and performance picks Safe mode, which locks audio processing while a preset loads, or the two unsafe modes, which load without locking it.
Menu — Arm mode on the SLOT port applies a slot pressed by hand on the next clock trigger arriving there.
Note — a red connection light means the module beside it is a different model from the one the presets were stored for.
Stores, recalls and sequences sixteen presets of one module, placed immediately to the right of the module it manages.
Short-press applies this preset to the managed module, or in write mode stores that module's current preset into it; long-press clears it, or sets the sequence length in read mode.
Read applies a preset by hand, Auto stores the current preset whenever a new slot is selected, and Write stores the managed module's preset into the slot pressed.
Selects the preset slot: a trigger steps through the slots forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, or 0-10V or a volt-per-octave note picks one outright.
A trigger restarts the preset sequence at the first slot.
Menu — the managed module can be taken from the left instead of the right.
Menu — Stability and performance picks Safe mode, which locks audio processing while a preset loads, or the two unsafe modes, which load without locking it.
Menu — Arm mode on the SLOT port applies a slot pressed by hand on the next clock trigger arriving there.
Note — a red connection light means the module beside it is a different model from the one the presets were stored for.
Sends and receives 64 channels of audio and CV to and from an audio device.
Carries a signal to one output channel of the audio device.
Carries the signal from one input channel of the audio device.
Menu — Master audio module makes this module drive Rack's engine timing.
Menu — DC blocker removes any constant offset from the signals leaving for the device.
Note — the audio device, its sample rate and its block size are picked on the display.
Turns MIDI notes and control changes from a controller into keyboard events, so a MIDI control can fire any Rack hotkey.
Menu — a mapping binds one MIDI note or control change to one key, with Ctrl, Alt and Shift available as modifiers.
Note — mappings are saved in the module's presets, so a set of them can be reused across patches.
Adds analogue-style defects to a polyphonic cable: noise, crosstalk between channels, crackle, pitch wobble, bit crushing and dropouts.
Adds a low level of white noise, at a different level on each channel.
Mixes a small amount of each channel of the polyphonic cable into its neighbours.
Adds random pops and crackles.
Adds occasional pitch wobble.
Adds occasional bit-depth and sample-rate reduction.
Adds occasional dropouts, which silence samples.
The polyphonic audio the defects are applied to.
The input with the switched-on defects applied, carrying the same number of channels.
Note — every instance generates its own defects, so two of these modules do not sound alike.
Virtual MIDI merger and splitter: it takes messages from two MIDI inputs and passes them to two MIDI outputs, filtering or rewriting the channel on the way.
Menu — an output set to Thru passes every message unchanged.
Menu — picking a MIDI channel for an output offers Replace, which rewrites the channel of every message, Filter, which passes only that channel, and Block, which passes everything but it.
Menu — each input can be filtered to one MIDI channel before its messages reach the outputs.
Note — system messages pass through unchanged in every mode.
Spreads the channels of a polyphonic cable across the stereo field, giving each channel its own random position.
Sets the widest random position allowed, 0% at the centre to 100% across the full stereo field, and attenuates the spread CV input.
Sets the widest random position allowed by voltage, 0-10V for the full stereo field, attenuated by the SPREAD knob; with nothing patched the module reads 10V here.
Moves the positions over time: negative settings drift each channel towards the side it was given, positive settings drift them towards the centre.
Sets each channel's position from an outside voltage, 0-10V, when the distribution is set to External; monophonic or polyphonic.
The polyphonic signal to be panned.
A trigger gives every channel a new random position; with a polyphonic trigger only the channels that receive one are moved.
Sets the level of both outputs, from silence to plus 6dB.
The left side of the panned signal, summed to one channel unless the menu keeps it polyphonic.
The right side of the panned signal, summed to one channel unless the menu keeps it polyphonic.
Menu — Distribution draws the random positions from a normal curve favouring the centre, a mirrored normal curve favouring the edges, an even spread, or the DIST input.
Logs incoming MIDI messages with their timing, and writes the log out as a text file.
Menu — Show engine frame replaces the elapsed-seconds stamp on each line with the last six digits of the engine frame number.
Menu — the log can be cleared, and SysEx data logging switched on and off.
Note — program change, song select, song pointer, SysEx and 14-bit CC, RPN and NRPN messages are all logged.
A digital distortion built on a bistable resonator: audio drives a resonant filter whose feedback path is nonlinear, and which can be pushed into self-oscillation.
Sets the gain before the resonator, -20dB to 20dB; higher settings give more saturation and push the resonator towards self-oscillation.
Sets the centre frequency of the resonator, 20Hz to 2000Hz.
Sets the damping of the resonator, -6 to -3; more negative settings give a longer, more ringing decay.
Sets the amount of nonlinear distortion in the resonator's feedback path, 0.1 to 1.
Sets the asymmetry of the nonlinearity, -1 to 1, biased towards compression below zero and towards expansion above it.
Sets the level after the resonator, -20dB to 20dB.
The polyphonic audio fed into the resonator.
The resonator output, carrying the same number of channels as the input.
One knob driving up to four mapped parameters and two CV outputs, each with its own scaling and slew.
Binds one parameter: press it, then click a knob, fader or switch on any module.
Sets the value sent to every mapped parameter and to both CV outputs, 0% to 100%, through the scaling set for each of them.
Carries the macro value as a voltage, through the scaling set for that output on its context menu.
Sets the macro value by voltage in place of the knob, which then attenuates it; 0-10V, or -5V to 5V on the menu.
Menu — each mapping slot and each output has its own slew and a pair of Low and High sliders scaling its range, which can also invert it.
Maps one parameter of another module onto four separate knobs, so several controllers can drive that parameter at once.
Binds a parameter to this group of four knobs: press it, then click a knob, fader or switch on any module.
Sets the bound parameter, and follows that parameter when it is changed elsewhere unless Read is switched off for this knob.
Morphs the parameters of other modules between up to twelve snapshots, fading from one to the next over a set time.
Short-press applies this snapshot to the bound parameters, or in write mode stores their current values into it; long-press clears it, or sets the sequence length in read mode.
Read morphs between snapshots as the CV input selects them, Auto stores the current values whenever a new snapshot is selected, and Write stores them into the snapshot pressed.
Sets how long a fade between snapshots takes, about 10ms at the bottom of its travel and about 10 seconds at the top, on an exponential curve.
Sets the curve of the fade: linear at the centre, easing in on one side and easing out on the other.
Adds to the fade time set by the knob or by the snapshot, one volt counting as a tenth of the knob's travel.
Selects the snapshot: a trigger steps through the slots forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, 0-10V or a note picks one outright, and Phase mode scans through them.
A trigger restarts the snapshot sequence at the first usable slot.
Carries a rising envelope during a fade, a gate while one runs, a trigger on a snapshot change or at the start or end of a fade, or all of these on separate polyphonic channels.
Menu — Bind module (left) binds every parameter of the module on the left, and Bind single parameter or Bind multiple parameters bind ones you click.
Menu — Set as first and Set as last on a snapshot button narrow the range of slots used for sequencing and CV selection.
Menu — Disable CV clamping lets the fade CV push the fade time past ten seconds, as far as several hours.
Note — fifteen +T expanders to the right raise the total number of snapshots to 192.
Expander adding twelve more snapshot slots to TRANSIT, placed immediately to the right of it or of another +T.
Short-press applies this snapshot to the parameters bound by TRANSIT, or in write mode stores their current values into it; long-press clears it.
TransitEx.notes: The single output carries no position in the census and no name; it is not drawn on the panel, so it has no line.

lines: Turns mouse-wheel movement and middle-mouse clicks into 10V triggers and gates.
Fires a 10V trigger on every step of the mouse wheel upwards.
Fires a 10V trigger on every step of the mouse wheel downwards.
Goes to 10V on a middle-mouse click, as a trigger, as a gate while the button is held, or as a level toggled by each click, set on the menu.
Limits capture of mouse-wheel and middle-click events to the times a parameter is hovered; switched off, they are caught wherever the mouse points.
Menu — modifier keys can be required before a mouse-wheel event is caught, which leaves plain scrolling free to move the Rack view.
Note — only the first instance with a given set of modifiers receives events, so further instances need different modifiers.
Turns hotkeys and extra mouse buttons into triggers and gates, and into commands for the view, cables and modules that Rack offers no other way to reach.
Carries 10V when the hotkey learned in this slot is pressed: a short trigger, a gate while the key is held, or a level toggled by each press; slots set to other commands carry nothing.
Menu — Learn on a slot binds the next hotkey or mouse button pressed, with Alt, Ctrl or Cmd and Shift shown on the lights.
Menu — the view commands zoom to the hovered module, to a learned module, or out to the whole patch, and scroll the view in each direction.
Menu — the parameter commands randomise the hovered parameter and copy and paste its value.
Menu — the module commands add a module with a preset, add a random module, save the hovered module's preset, and send a learned hotkey to a learned module.
Menu — the cable commands toggle cable opacity and visibility, step the hovered cable to the next colour or a chosen one, and rotate the order of stacked cables.
Note — a hotkey assigned to two slots works in only one of them.
Jumps the Rack view to any of ten saved places in the patch, restoring the zoom level saved with each of them.
Short-press jumps the view to what this slot holds; long-press binds the module clicked next, or clears the slot when one is already bound.
Fires the jump points by voltage: the first ten channels of a polyphonic cable fire points one to ten, or the menu takes notes C5 to A5 on a monophonic cable.
Menu — Learn current selection on a jump point binds every module currently selected, rather than a single one.
Menu — Jump position centres the bound modules on screen or puts them in the top-left corner, and Ignore zoom level keeps the current zoom.
Note — Shift with the number keys 1 to 0 fires the jump points, until a cable is patched to the input.
Puts small text labels on modules and cables in the patch, keeping each label attached to what it names as that is moved.
Arms labelling: press it, then click a module to put a new label on it.
Locks the labels so they cannot be moved or edited; unlocked, a label can be dragged within its module and edited from its own context menu.
Raises the opacity of every label by 5%.
Lowers the opacity of every label by 5%.
Hides every label while it is switched on.
Menu — Label appearance sets what new labels are given: size from 8 to 24 pixels, width from 20 to 180 pixels, opacity, rotation, colour, font and font colour.
Menu — Consolidate GLUE moves the labels of every other GLUE in the patch into this one and removes those modules.
Note — a label can be dragged half its module's width past the module's edge, and is drawn above the module but below the cables.
Holds up to 32 parameters of other modules at fixed values, so they cannot be changed by mouse or by the Randomize menu item.
Starts binding: press it, then click a knob, fader, switch or button to lock it at its current value.
Menu — the list of locked parameters is on the context menu, and each one can be released from there.
Note — locked parameters survive a STRIP file as long as this module is part of the strip.
Adds a voltage offset to each channel of a polyphonic cable, one knob per channel, sixteen channels in all.
Sets the offset added to that channel, as an exact voltage, in semitone steps of a twelfth of a volt, or in whole volts, as set on the menu.
The polyphonic signal the offsets are added to; with nothing patched the knobs produce the output on their own.
The input with each channel's offset added.
Menu — Channels sets how many channels the output carries; on Auto it matches the number arriving at the input.
Adds a voltage offset to each channel of a polyphonic cable, one knob per channel, eight channels in all.
Sets the offset added to that channel, as an exact voltage, in semitone steps of a twelfth of a volt, or in whole volts, as set on the menu.
The polyphonic signal the offsets are added to; with nothing patched the knobs produce the output on their own.
The input with each channel's offset added.
Menu — Channels sets how many channels the output carries; on Auto it matches the number arriving at the input.
Keeps the parameters of several instances of the same module in step, so a change to one of them changes all of them.
Drives one parameter of the mirrored modules with 0-10V; which parameter this port reaches is assigned on its context menu.
Menu — Bind source module (left) takes every parameter of the module on the left, Map module (right) links the module on the other side, and Add and map new module adds one.
Menu — Sync module presets copies the source module's whole preset to the mirrored modules, which covers internal state that parameters do not reach.
Note — once bound, the mirrored modules can be moved anywhere in the patch.
Reads the relative protocols of endless rotary knobs on a MIDI controller and turns each twist of a knob into triggers.
Fires a trigger each time the MIDI control assigned to this jack is turned up.
Fires a trigger each time the MIDI control assigned to this jack is turned down.
Menu — polyphonic mode sends all sixteen channels on the first increment and decrement jacks instead of using eight jacks for each.
Menu — the protocol is picked to match the controller, covering Native Instruments, Arturia Beatstep, Behringer X-TOUCH Mini, Midi Fighter Twister, Akai MPD218 and Hercules DJControl Starlight.
Turns increment and decrement triggers into an absolute voltage, adding or subtracting a fixed step on each trigger.
Sets exponential slew on the output, 0 to 5 seconds; patching the slew input takes this knob out of use.
Sets the voltage each trigger adds or subtracts, 0 to 5V.
Sets the slew of the output by voltage, 0-5V, in place of the SLEW knob.
A trigger adds one step to the output voltage.
A trigger subtracts one step from the output voltage.
Sets the output to the voltage present here, and again on every change of that voltage.
The accumulated voltage, clamped to the range picked on the menu: 0-5V, 0-10V, -5V to 5V or -10V to 10V.
Turns increment and decrement triggers into an absolute voltage on each of sixteen polyphonic channels, adding or subtracting a fixed step on each trigger.
Sets exponential slew on the output, 0 to 5 seconds; patching the slew input takes this knob out of use.
Sets the voltage each trigger adds or subtracts, 0 to 5V.
Sets the slew of the output by voltage, 0-5V, in place of the SLEW knob.
A trigger adds one step to the output voltage of that channel; polyphonic.
A trigger subtracts one step from the output voltage of that channel; polyphonic.
A trigger resets the output to 0V, or to the voltage at the VOLT input when a cable is patched there; monophonic.
Sets the voltage the output is reset to; polyphonic, and normalled to its first channel.
The accumulated voltage for each channel, clamped to the range picked on the menu: 0-5V, 0-10V, -5V to 5V or -10V to 10V.
Controls whatever parameter the mouse pointer is over, by voltage, by triggers or from a MIDI control.
While this gate is high, changes made to the hovered parameter are ten times finer; holding Shift does the same.
Smooths the changes made to the hovered parameter, 0 to 5 seconds.
Sets the smoothing of changes to the hovered parameter by voltage, in place of the SLEW knob.
Sets how far each trigger moves the hovered parameter, 0% to 20% of that parameter's full range.
A trigger moves the hovered parameter up by one step.
A trigger moves the hovered parameter down by one step.
Sets the hovered parameter: in Differential mode each change of voltage is added to the parameter, in Absolute mode 0-10V maps onto its full range. A cable on INC or DEC leaves this port unread.
Carries the value of the hovered parameter as a voltage; on Reduced only changes made by this module update it, on Full every change to the parameter does.
Note — several instances with different step sizes, or one with the fine gate held high, give coarse and fine control from different MIDI knobs.
Sail.notes: The manual calls the fine-adjustment port MOD and describes it as raising the precision of the IN port in Differential mode; the maker's own tooltip ties it to the INC and DEC inputs. The panel prints FINE.

lines: An eight by eight matrix mixer: each pad routes one input into one output, with an attenuverter on every output and eight scenes that crossfade into one another.
Routes that input into that output while it is lit, fading in and out over the times set by the two fade trimpots.
Silences that output whatever the pads feeding it are set to.
Short-press loads that scene, or stores the current matrix, input modes and output settings into it; long-press clears it.
Scales that output from -2 to 2, inverting it below zero.
Sets how long a signal takes to fade in when its pad is switched on, within the maximum fade time picked on the menu.
Sets how long a signal takes to fade out when its pad is switched off, within the maximum fade time picked on the menu.
Held high, selects that input column so that a trigger on a row button toggles the pad where the two cross; it exists so the matrix can be driven by MIDI mapping.
A trigger toggles the pad where this output row crosses the input column currently held high; it exists so the matrix can be driven by MIDI mapping.
One of the signals routed into the matrix; polyphonic, and its context menu can replace it with a constant voltage instead.
Selects the scene: a trigger steps through them forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, or 0-10V or a volt-per-octave note picks one outright.
A trigger restarts the scene selection at the first scene.
The sum of every input whose pad in that row is lit, scaled by that row's attenuverter; polyphonic.
Menu — an input's mode is Off, Direct, Linear fade, or one of the constant voltages from minus twelve to plus twelve cents, for adding musical intervals.
Menu — Scene lock keeps the scene and output buttons working while stopping the matrix pads from being edited.
Menu — Channels sets how many polyphonic channels are processed, one to sixteen, and Limit output clamps each output to -10V to 10V.
Intermix.notes: The eight signal inputs and eight mix outputs carry whatever is patched into them, audio or CV, so they are left uncoloured.

lines: Expander for INTERMIX, placed immediately to the right of it, setting a separate crossfade time for each output.
Sets the crossfade time applied to the signal reaching that output when scenes change.
Menu — the maximum fade time is 4 seconds, 15 seconds or 60 seconds, and defaults to 15 seconds.
Note — detaching the expander, or pointing it at a different input column, returns every fade time to the value set on INTERMIX itself.
IntermixFade.notes: The manual describes this expander as holding a fade-in and a fade-out time for every pad of one selected input column; the module carries one knob per row and the maker's tooltips describe them per output. Both readings are recorded here rather than one being picked.

lines: Expander for INTERMIX, placed immediately to the right of it, turning the fades of one selected input column into envelopes.
Carries a 0-10V envelope following the fade of the selected input column into that output, or a plain gate where that input is not set to linear fade.
Expander for INTERMIX, placed immediately to the right of it, reporting which of the outputs are carrying anything.
Goes to 10V while at least one input is routed into that output.
A four-channel ratcheting sequencer whose playheads move across a shared square grid, raising a trigger and a voltage on each filled cell they enter.
A trigger moves the yellow playhead one cell along its current direction.
A trigger moves that playhead one cell along its current direction; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's clock, unless normalling is switched off on the menu.
A trigger returns the yellow playhead to its start cell, which is set by dragging it while the grid is in edit mode.
A trigger returns that playhead to its start cell; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's reset, unless normalling is switched off on the menu.
A trigger turns the yellow playhead 90 degrees to the right, or 180 degrees when its context menu is set that way.
A trigger turns that playhead 90 degrees to the right, or 180 degrees when its context menu is set that way; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's turn input.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the left, relative to the direction each is travelling.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the right, relative to the direction each is travelling.
Fires a trigger each time that playhead enters a filled cell, or a burst of ratchets on a half-filled one.
Carries the voltage stored in the cell that playhead last triggered on, within the range set for that channel, 0-3V by default.
Menu — the grid is sized from 2 by 2 up to 32 by 32, and its cells can be randomised, with or without half-filled cells.
Menu — edit mode lets each playhead's start cell be dragged, while the sequencer keeps running.
Menu — a playhead's ratcheting can be switched off, limited to even numbers, to multiples of three or to powers of two, with a probability setting favouring longer bursts.
Note — clicking a cell steps it through off, filled and half-filled, and gives it a new random voltage each time.
Maze.notes: The single parameter carries no position in the census and is not drawn on the panel, so it has no line.

lines: A four-channel ratcheting sequencer whose playheads move across a shared hexagonal grid, raising a trigger and a voltage on each filled cell they enter.
A trigger moves the yellow playhead one cell along its current direction.
A trigger moves that playhead one cell along its current direction; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's clock, unless normalling is switched off on the menu.
A trigger returns the yellow playhead to its start cell, which is set by dragging it while the grid is in edit mode.
A trigger returns that playhead to its start cell; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's reset, unless normalling is switched off on the menu.
A trigger turns the yellow playhead by 60 degrees, 120 degrees, alternating 60 and 120, or 180 degrees, as its context menu is set.
A trigger turns that playhead by the angle picked on its context menu; with nothing patched it follows the yellow channel's turn input, unless normalling is switched off.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the left and upwards, relative to the direction each is travelling.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the left and downwards, relative to the direction each is travelling.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the right and upwards, relative to the direction each is travelling.
A trigger shifts every playhead one lane to the right and downwards, relative to the direction each is travelling.
Fires a trigger each time that playhead enters a filled cell, or a burst of ratchets on a half-filled one.
Carries the voltage stored in the cell that playhead last triggered on, within the range set for that channel, 0-3V by default.
Menu — the grid is sized by its radius in cells, and can be randomised, with or without half-filled cells.
Menu — edit mode lets each playhead's start cell be dragged, while the sequencer keeps running.
Menu — a playhead's ratcheting can be switched off, limited to even numbers, to multiples of three or to powers of two, with a probability setting favouring longer bursts.
Note — clicking a cell steps it through off, filled and half-filled, and gives it a new random voltage each time.
Hive.notes: The single parameter carries no position in the census and is not drawn on the panel, so it has no line.

lines: A two-dimensional mixer: eight inputs and four mix outputs are placed on an XY field, and each input feeds a mix output by how close the two are on that field.
The monophonic source for that channel.
Sets that input's place along the horizontal axis of the field.
Moves that input along the horizontal axis of the field, added to its position knob and scaled by the attenuverter for this port.
Scales the horizontal position CV for that input, -1 to 1, inverting it below zero and silencing it at the centre.
Sets that input's place along the vertical axis of the field.
Moves that input along the vertical axis of the field, added to its position knob and scaled by the attenuverter for this port.
Scales the vertical position CV for that input, -1 to 1, inverting it below zero and silencing it at the centre.
Modulates that input's radius, its amount, its horizontal or vertical offset, or sends it on a random walk, as picked on that channel's display menu.
Scales the modulation CV for that input, -1 to 1, inverting it below zero and silencing it at the centre.
Carries that input scaled by its amount and by its distance to each mix output, combined in the output mode picked on that channel's display menu, despite the tooltip calling it a direct output.
Sets the level of that mix output, 0% to 200%.
Sets that mix output's place along the horizontal axis of the field.
Moves that mix output along the horizontal axis of the field, scaled by the attenuverter for this port.
Scales the horizontal position CV for that mix output, -1 to 1, inverting it below zero and silencing it at the centre.
Sets that mix output's place along the vertical axis of the field.
Moves that mix output along the vertical axis of the field, scaled by the attenuverter for this port.
Scales the vertical position CV for that mix output, -1 to 1, inverting it below zero and silencing it at the centre.
Selects which of that mix output's sixteen motion sequences is followed: a trigger steps forward, reverse or at random, or 0-10V or notes C4 to D sharp 5 pick one outright.
Sets how far that mix output has travelled along its motion sequence, the input voltage mapping onto the length of the sequence.
The mix of every input whose radius reaches that output's place on the field, scaled by that output's volume.
Menu — the number of active input channels is set from 1 to 8 and the number of mix channels from 1 to 4.
Menu — an input's own display menu sets its amount, its radius, the voltage range of its position CVs, what its modulation port reaches, and how its direct output is combined.
Menu — an output mode scales each mix contribution to at most one part in the number of mix ports, limits it to 100%, clips it, or folds it at -5V to 5V or 0-10V.
Note — a motion sequence is recorded by clicking the mix channel's number display, then dragging on the field; preset paths such as circles, saws and spirals are on the same menu.
Arena.notes: Parameter indices 32 to 47, 56 to 71 and 88 to 91 are configured with no name and no panel position; they are not drawn on the panel and have no line. The amount and radius sliders on each channel are drawn by the module rather than being parameters. The maker's tooltip calls the per-input OUT jack a direct output of the channel's audio, while the manual says it is scaled by the amount and by the distances to the mix ports; the manual's account is used here.

lines: Runs a knockout tournament between up to sixteen signals: each trigger draws a random winner of every one-on-one match until one signal is left.
One of the sixteen signals entered in the tournament.
Carries the winner of one first-round match between two of the inputs.
Carries the winner of one second-round match between two first-round winners.
Carries the winner of one third-round match between two second-round winners.
Carries the signal that won all four rounds.
Starts a new contest, drawing a fresh set of winners.
Inverts the result, so every loser of a match becomes its winner and every winner becomes its loser.
A trigger starts a new contest, drawing a fresh set of winners.
A trigger inverts the result of every match.
Menu — CV / Audio routes the winning signal straight through, Sample & Hold captures one sample of each input on a trigger, and Quantum mixes every input by weight instead of picking one.
Note — a green light marks a winning signal, a red one an inverted state, and white lights show the weighting in Quantum mode.
FourRounds.notes: The sixteen contest inputs and the winner outputs carry whatever is patched in, audio or CV, so they are left uncoloured.

lines: A serial-in parallel-out shift register: each trigger samples the input into a register of 4096 cells, and sixteen output channels read back cells picked by SKIP and INCR.
A trigger samples the input signal and stores it in the next cell of the register.
Sets how far back in the register output channel 1 reads, 0 to 127 cells; at 0 the module behaves as a plain shift register.
Adds to the number of cells output channel 1 reads back, 0-10V mapping onto 0 to 127 cells.
Sets how many further cells back each output channel reads than the channel before it, 0 to 7; at 0 every channel reads the same spacing as a plain shift register.
Adds to the spacing between output channels, 0-10V mapping onto 0 to 7 cells.
The monophonic signal sampled into the register.
Sixteen channels carrying the register cells picked out by SKIP and INCR.
Maps MIDI control changes and notes onto the parameters of any modules, with a large mapping table, pickup modes, note mapping, slew, input scaling and MIDI feedback.
Menu — the input mode of a CC slot is Direct, which applies every message, or one of the two pickup modes, which ignore messages until the control reaches the parameter's value.
Menu — Pickup (snap) keeps a control locked to its parameter until the parameter is changed from inside Rack, while Pickup (jump) also releases it when the control jumps by more than 7%.
Menu — the note mode of a slot sets the parameter to its maximum on a note, maps velocity onto its range, or toggles it between minimum and maximum on each note.
Menu — Map module (left) binds every parameter of the module on the left, and Map module (select) binds the parameters of a module you click.
Menu — Locate and indicate stops incoming MIDI changing parameters, and instead centres the mapped module on screen and flashes its indicator.
Menu — 14-bit CC pairs control changes 0 to 31 with 32 to 63, raising the resolution of a slot from 0-127 to 0-16383.
Menu — each slot has its own slew and a pair of Low and High sliders scaling the incoming MIDI value, which can also invert the control.
Menu — MIDI feedback sends a parameter's value back to the controller on the same CC or note, and can be re-sent by hand or twice a second.
Maps MIDI control changes and notes onto the parameters of any modules, with pickup modes, note mapping, slew, input scaling and MIDI feedback to the controller.
Menu — the input mode of a CC slot is Direct, which applies every message, or one of the two pickup modes, which ignore messages until the control reaches the parameter's value.
Menu — Pickup (snap) keeps a control locked to its parameter until the parameter is changed from inside Rack, while Pickup (jump) also releases it when the control jumps by more than 7%.
Menu — the note mode of a slot sets the parameter to its maximum on a note, maps velocity onto its range, or toggles it between minimum and maximum on each note.
Menu — Map module (left) binds every parameter of the module on the left, and Map module (select) binds the parameters of a module you click.
Menu — Locate and indicate stops incoming MIDI changing parameters, and instead centres the mapped module on screen and flashes its indicator.
Menu — 14-bit CC pairs control changes 0 to 31 with 32 to 63, raising the resolution of a slot from 0-127 to 0-16383.
Menu — each slot has its own slew and a pair of Low and High sliders scaling the incoming MIDI value, which can also invert the control.
Menu — MIDI feedback sends a parameter's value back to the controller on the same CC or note, and can be re-sent by hand or twice a second.
Expander for MIDI-CAT, placed immediately to the right of it, adding fine adjustment of the parameters MIDI-CAT has mapped.
While this gate is high, a mapped MIDI control moves its parameter within a 10% range, once that control has been returned to its centre.
While this gate is high, a mapped MIDI control moves its parameter within a 1, 2 or 5% range, once that control has been returned to its centre.
Note — fine adjustment works on CC mappings whose input mode is Pickup (snap) or Pickup (jump).
Expander for MIDI-CAT, placed immediately to the right of it, adding four clocks that hold incoming MIDI back until the next beat.
A trigger applies the MIDI messages buffered since the previous trigger to the parameters assigned to this clock.
Menu — instant feedback sends the MIDI reply as the message arrives, and deferred feedback sends it on the clock trigger that applies the value.
Expander for MIDI-CAT, placed immediately to the right of it, giving that MIDI-CAT a name of up to eight characters which a parameter's own context menu can address.
Starts MIDI mapping on the first empty slot of MIDI-CAT.
Expander for MIDI-CAT, placed immediately to the right of it, storing one MIDI mapping for each type of module so a mapping can be recalled without being made again.
Turns the cursor into a crosshair; clicking a module loads the stored mapping for that type of module into MIDI-CAT.
Scans the patch backwards and applies the stored mapping of the previous module that has one.
Scans the patch forwards and applies the stored mapping of the next module that has one.
A trigger applies the stored mapping of the previous module in the patch that has one.
A trigger applies the stored mapping of the next module in the patch that has one.
Menu — Store mapping saves the mapping currently in MIDI-CAT under the type of module it was made for, and Delete removes one.
Menu — a restriction list limits which modules the scanning buttons consider; with it empty every module in the patch is considered.
Note — the stored mappings are held in this module, so exporting its preset carries them to other patches.
Imports a Rack selection file or the clipboard into the patch, keeping parameter mappings and GLUE labels intact.
Menu — Import reads a .vcvs file and shows the selection under the cursor, where a left-click places it and a right-click cancels.
Menu — Paste from Clipboard places a selection held in the clipboard the same way.
Note — the module takes no part in saving, works with any .vcvs file, and can be removed once the import is done.
Provides four named patch points inside a STRIP, so cables to the rest of the patch stay connected while different strips are loaded.
Carries whatever is patched here to the matching output of another STRIP-BAY bearing the same text identifier.
Carries what is patched into the matching input of another STRIP-BAY bearing the same text identifier.
Note — two STRIP-BAY modules are paired by typing the same text identifier into both.
Manages the row of modules beside it as a group: it disables, randomises, saves, loads, copies and pastes them together.
Cycles which modules are managed: those on both sides, those on the left only, or those on the right only, shown by the triangular lights.
Enables the managed modules, or toggles them between enabled and disabled, depending on the mode picked on the menu.
Enables the managed modules; the menu sets whether this port acts on a trigger, as a toggle, or by gate level.
Disables the managed modules.
A trigger disables the managed modules.
Randomises the managed modules.
A trigger randomises the managed modules, following the include and exclude list.
Hold it to enter parameter learn mode, then click parameters to include them in or exclude them from randomisation.
Menu — a strip is saved as a .vcvss file holding every module's settings, the cables between them and their parameter mappings, and Load with replace clears the row first.
Menu — Randomize parameters only leaves each module's internal state untouched.
Note — a strip is the unbroken row of modules next to this one; leaving a gap in the row is what sets its extent.
Replaces or adds individual channels inside a polyphonic cable, using monophonic cables for up to sixteen of them.
The polyphonic signal passed through to the output.
Replaces that channel of the polyphonic signal, or adds it when the polyphonic input carries fewer channels than that.
The polyphonic input with each patched monophonic channel put in its place.
Replaces or adds individual channels inside a polyphonic cable, using monophonic cables for up to eight of them.
The polyphonic signal passed through to the output.
Replaces that channel of the polyphonic signal, or adds it when the polyphonic input carries fewer channels than that.
The polyphonic input with each patched monophonic channel put in its place.
Applies a boolean function to up to four inputs across sixteen polyphonic channels, with the function selectable by CV and a sample and hold on the result.
Steps to the next boolean function, in the order AND, NOR, XOR, OR and NAND.
A trigger makes the module hold its result until the next trigger; with nothing patched the output follows the inputs continuously. Polyphonic and normalled to its first channel.
Selects the boolean function: a trigger steps to the next one, or 0-10V in five steps of 2V, or notes C4 to E4, as set on the menu. Monophonic.
One of the four signals the boolean function is applied to; read as high from 1.0V and low below it. Polyphonic, with only connected channels counted.
Carries 10V while the boolean function is true and 0V while it is false, or a 1ms trigger when it turns true or on any change of the result, as set on the menu.
Records the movements of one mapped parameter into up to eight sequences and plays them back, with direct phase control and several recording modes.
Starts and stops recording of the mapped parameter; in touch and move modes it arms recording, which then begins on the first move of the parameter.
Steps to the previous sequence, wrapping round at the first.
Steps to the next sequence, wrapping round at the last.
Smooths the played-back curve and the jumps at the end of a sequence or on a change of sequence.
Starts and stops playback of the selected sequence.
Returns playback to the start of the selected sequence.
Selects the sequence: 0-10V split into eight bands, notes C4 to G4, or a trigger stepping to the next, as set on the menu.
Sets the playback position directly, 0-10V mapping onto the length of the sequence; a cable here disables the run and reset buttons and ports.
Starts and stops playback, as a gate or as a trigger, set on the menu.
A trigger returns playback to the start of the selected sequence.
Starts and stops recording, as a gate or as a trigger set on the menu; in touch and move modes it only arms recording.
Carries a gate while recording runs, or a trigger when recording starts and stops, as set on the menu.
Records this voltage as the automation in place of the parameter's movements, 0-10V or -5V to 5V on the menu.
Carries the played-back voltage, 0-10V or -5V to 5V, or a trigger each time playback reaches the end of a sequence, as set on the menu.
Menu — a sample rate from 15Hz to 2kHz and a count of one, two, four or eight sequences divide a store of 64k samples between them; changing either erases every recording.
Menu — the recording mode starts on the first click on the parameter, on its first change, on the record button itself, or captures a single value and holds it.
Menu — the play mode loops one sequence, plays it once, ping-pongs it, loops through all of them, or walks through them at random.
Note — every port is monophonic, and recording needs a parameter to be mapped even when the IN port is used.
Spreads a carrier signal across up to sixteen polyphonic output channels, the modulator voltage deciding which channels it reaches and in what proportion.
Sets which output channels the carrier reaches: 0-10V is divided by the number of active channels, and within each division the carrier crossfades from one channel to the next. Monophonic.
The signal spread across the output channels; with nothing patched a constant 10V is used. Monophonic.
A polyphonic signal whose channel is sent to the matching output channel, attenuverted by the carrier level on that channel; unconnected channels are ignored.
Sets how many output channels the carrier is spread over, 2 to 16.
Shifts the block of active channels up the polyphonic cable, by 0 to 14 channels.
The polyphonic result, one channel for each active channel.
Attaches to up to 32 parameters of any modules and puts out a voltage that follows each one as it moves.
Carries the values of mapping slots 1 to 16 on sixteen polyphonic channels.
Carries the values of mapping slots 17 to 32 on sixteen polyphonic channels.
Menu — Lock mapping slots prevents accidental changes to the slot list and stops it swallowing mouse scrolling.
Menu — Audio rate processing off updates the outputs every 32nd sample instead of every sample.
Adds CV control of one parameter of any module, with offset, scaling and an output following that parameter.
Binds a parameter: press it, then click a knob, fader or switch on any module.
Sets the mapped parameter; 0-10V, or -5V to 5V on the menu.
Sets the offset added to the input, 0-10V mapping onto 0% to 100%, and takes the offset trimpot out of use.
Offsets the input by 0% to 100% of its range.
Sets the scaling of the input, -10V to 10V mapping onto -200% to 200%, and takes the scale trimpot out of use.
Scales the input from -200% to 200%.
Carries the value of the mapped parameter as a voltage, in the range picked for the input port, and inverted when the menu says so.
Adds CV control to up to 32 parameters of any modules, taking the voltages from two polyphonic inputs.
The sixteen channels feeding mapping slots 1 to 16; 0-10V, or -5V to 5V on the menu.
The sixteen channels feeding mapping slots 17 to 32; 0-10V, or -5V to 5V on the menu.
Menu — each mapping slot has its own slew and a pair of Low and High sliders scaling the incoming voltage, which can also invert it.
Menu — Unlock lets a mapped parameter be moved by hand for as long as its input voltage does not change.
Menu — any input channel can be routed to any mapping slot, and each channel can be given a text label.
Menu — Audio rate processing off updates mapped parameters every 32nd sample instead of every sample.
Expander for CV-MAP, placed immediately to the right of it, giving that CV-MAP a name of up to eight characters which a parameter's own context menu can address.
Note — the name lets a parameter be mapped or re-mapped to a chosen input channel from the parameter's own context menu.
Sets the appearance of the on-screen overlay that MIDI-CAT and SAIL show on parameter changes, and adds a magnifying loupe around the mouse pointer.
Menu — the overlay settings apply to every module that draws the overlay, not to this module alone.
Menu — the magnifier has a learned hotkey, a radius in pixels and a zoom factor, and shows while that hotkey is held.
Replaces Rack's module browser with the browser from Rack v0.6, or with modified versions of the v1 and v2 browsers carrying favourites, custom tags, width filtering and a preview loupe.
Menu — Auto-generate custom tags assigns tags from a curated rule set of about seventy categories by matching keywords against module names and descriptions.
Menu — Determine width for all modules measures every installed module's panel in HP, which fills the width filter without browsing to each module first.
Menu — favourites, hidden modules and custom tags are kept in the Rack user folder and can be exported and imported.
Note — in the v2 mod browser the width button cycles a chosen HP value through exact, that width or narrower, that width or wider, and off.
